detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, Warm high-summer palette of gold ripe wheat, red road dust and deep green pine, hard blue shadow under a clear bleached sky; the Utah valley and Salt Lake City, June 1860; American frontier, sunlight and lamplight only., 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:04. The shot begins from <Picture 4>: a full shot of the mustang up on its hind legs in the packed drove, Lucy thrown back along its neck with the straw hat swung back on its ribbon, her hair loose, the horns of the bullocks crowded round its forelegs, red dust to her stirrup. The camera is on the road beside the herd at the height of a mounted man's eye, four long strides from the horse. The camera tilts up with the rearing horse across the whole shot, travelling a head's height as the mustang goes up and tosses its head against the bit, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 Lucy comes forward along its neck and takes a fresh grip on the reins, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him Six wild-looking herdsmen on ponies ride the flanks of the drove at a normal walking pace swinging coiled ropes, and two more sit their horses at the corral rail watching the road., from 00:00 to 00:04. By 00:04, the mustang's head and Lucy's shoulders stand at the top of the frame with the crowded horns carried out below the bottom edge.
[Shot 2] From 00:04 to 00:08. At 00:04 the shot cuts to a medium two-shot at the mustang's head, beginning from <Picture 5>: a sinewy brown hand closed on the curb below the horse's jaw, <Subject 2> beside it on the powerful roan in the broad brown sombrero and the fringed buckskin, Lucy above on the mustang with her hair over her face. The camera pushes in on the two of them across the whole shot, travelling two long strides as <Subject 2> draws the mustang's head down and round toward his knee, from 00:04 to 00:07. <Subject 2> (S1), on screen, a tall, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] You're not hurt, I hope, miss.</d> His mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:07, as the line ends, Lucy lifts her face out of her hair and looks down at his hand, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot. Behind him Six wild-looking herdsmen on ponies ride the flanks of the drove at a normal walking pace swinging coiled ropes, and two more sit their horses at the corral rail watching the road., from 00:04 to 00:08. By 00:08, both riders stand half again as large with the horses' heads filling the bottom of the frame and the herd carried out past both edges.
